newsitem.title: USA: International Multifoods sees lower net.
newsitem.headline: International Multifoods sees lower net.

text.p: International Multifoods Corp said Tuesday it expects earnings for fiscal 1997 likely will be less than a year ago.

"While the problems in the vending distribution are being aggressively addressed, performance in that business is such that full-year earnings for the company overall are likely to be less than last year in spite of significant progress in the remainder of the distribution businesses, Venezuela Foods and the bakery segments," Robert Price, chairman, said in a statement.

Regarding the search for a new chief executive officer, Price added, "The board is in the process of interviewing candidates for the position of CEO and believes that a new CEO will be in place before the end of the fiscal year."
Earlier, International Multifoods reported second quarter earnings of $0.22 a share compared with year-ago earnings after unusual items of $0.38.
Price said International Multifoods' results overall in the second quarter exceeded expectations as a result of strong performance in MONACA, its Venezuela Foods operation.
Price said the year-to-year decrease in second-quarter earnings was primarily related to an operating loss in the vending distribution business.

International Multifoods said net sales in its foodservice distribution business were $432.7 million, up from $400.3 million. Earnings were $418,000, down from $3.8 million a year ago before unusual items.

The company said the increase in sales was primarily related to the addition of several new customer accounts in its limited-menu distribution business, as well as the acquisition of Alum Rock Foodservice in July 1995.
Earnings in this segment fell due to the vending business.

International Multifoods said second quarter net sales in its bakery division rose to $114.4 million from $110.1 million a year ago. Bakery earnings declined to $3.6 million from $4.7 million due to lower commercial bakery volumes that resulted from softness in a large customer's business and a strike at two large Canadian retailers.
Venezuela Foods' second quarter net sales were $87.4 million, down from $106.3 million a year ago. Earnings were $8.9 million, up five percent from $8.5 million last year.

Earnings in the Venezuela Foods segment benefited from strong volumes in corn flour and from a relatively stable exchange rate during the quarter. Sales were affected by volume declines in commercial wheat flour and agricultural products.

The economic stability and declining monthly inflation rates that have occurred in Venezuela since the government enacted major economic reforms in April provide a much improved business climate, the company said. The company said it continues to believe that full-year results for MONACA should exceed last year's.
